cluster_decisions.reason: Same generic title, but 2837 uniquely adds Pancreatic Cysts. Pediatric scope cannot be inferred.
Pediatric pancreas variants share core diagnoses but retain hereditary/genetic/recurrent, replacement therapy, nutritional and diagnostic requirements.
Exact pair 3326/3488 is embedded in a broader adrenal profile group with steroid therapy, hormonal evaluation and hormone monitoring.
Pediatric endocrine hubs differ in age scope, preventive care, nutrition, monitoring, diabetes technology and research; larger ID does not prove supersession.
Both pediatric rheumatology hubs compose shared capabilities; 3900 adds Biological Therapy.
Ophthalmology hubs share AI/twin/imaging but differ in surgery/telemedicine versus genetics/laboratory; version order unproven.
Exact pair 3340/3500 is only a subset of the larger same-title cluster. 3880 has distinct monitoring/research content.
Clinic/physician/telemedicine appointment workflow is shared; infectious disease, ENT and dermatology retain distinct specialty eligibility.
Shared CDS orchestration with separate clinical contexts and evaluation; endocrine profile uniquely calls Digital Twin.
Provider organization directory and search data ownership can be shared while specialty profiles and search views remain separate.
Identical title and parsed body; four pancreatic requirements retained verbatim for both IDs.
Identical title and parsed body; four adrenal requirements retained for both IDs.
Identical title and body; all eight integration requirements retained.
The abbreviated 95 contains no requirement beyond 36. Textual intent equivalence only; broader corpus/context still needs reconciliation.
distinct: 36 adds age/weight/labs, renal/hepatic safety, monitoring and unsafe legacy recommendations that need correction.

cluster_decisions.reason: Persistence schema, patient workflow and AI-labelled dynamic/cross-border feature share one authorization domain but have distinct responsibilities.
Core model orchestration vs umbrella platform composition. No evidence that the latter supersedes the former.
Catalog/reported use/order/workflow cannot be merged into one clinical fact.
Different physiological and disease contexts use one twin core. Cardiology and respiratory integration expand model concerns with progression/prediction.
One policy engine, specialty-sensitive profiles; age/assent/jurisdiction plus reproductive/mental-health segmentation must survive.
Renal exchange adds dialysis/transplant/pathology and freshness to shared interoperability; not semantic duplicate.
